# Copilot instructions for InventoryFlow

- Architecture: 4 layers (Entities, DataAccess, Business, WinForms UI). EF Core + FluentValidation. UI is deliberately thin and talks only to Business services, never DALs.
- Build/run: InventoryFlow.UI targets net8.0-windows; other projects are net8.0 libraries. Build with `dotnet build InventoryFlow.sln`; run UI with `dotnet run --project InventoryFlow.UI/InventoryFlow.UI.csproj`.
- Service wiring: No DI container. [InventoryFlow.Business/DependencyResolvers/InstanceFactory.cs](../InventoryFlow.Business/DependencyResolvers/InstanceFactory.cs) manually news managers with Ef*Dal. When adding a feature: define interface + manager + validator + EfDal, then register in InstanceFactory.
- EF context: [InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Concrete/EntityFramework/InventoryContext.cs](../InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Concrete/EntityFramework/InventoryContext.cs) points to (localdb) InventoryFlowDB and configures Product.UnitPrice and Sale.TotalPrice as decimal(18,2). DbSet<Product> lives after OnConfiguring.
- Repository base: [InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Concrete/EntityFramework/EfEntityRepositoryBase.cs](../InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Concrete/EntityFramework/EfEntityRepositoryBase.cs) uses a fresh DbContext per call for Add/Delete/Get/GetAll/Update.
- Product flow: [InventoryFlow.Business/Concrete/ProductManager.cs](../InventoryFlow.Business/Concrete/ProductManager.cs) validates with ProductValidator, stamps AddedDate, and delegates persistence to IProductDal. GetProductsByProductName lowercases for case-insensitive search.
- Product projections: [InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Concrete/EntityFramework/EfProductDal.cs](../InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Concrete/EntityFramework/EfProductDal.cs) joins Categories into ProductDetailDto. GetProductDetailsByName uses SQL Contains without lowercasing (collation determines case sensitivity).
- Sale flow: [InventoryFlow.Business/Concrete/SaleManager.cs](../InventoryFlow.Business/Concrete/SaleManager.cs) validates quantity, pulls product via IProductService, enforces stock, decrements stock via Update, computes TotalPrice and Date, then saves via ISaleDal.
- Sale projections: [InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Concrete/EntityFramework/EfSaleDal.cs](../InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Concrete/EntityFramework/EfSaleDal.cs) joins product/category and left-joins customers; null customer renders as "Walk-in Customer" in SaleDetailDto.
- DTOs: ProductDetailDto and SaleDetailDto live in InventoryFlow.Entities/DTOs for grid binding (names/category/customer).
- Validation: Rules under InventoryFlow.Business/ValidationRules (e.g., ProductValidator, SaleValidator) and executed via [InventoryFlow.Business/Utilities/ValidationTool.cs](../InventoryFlow.Business/Utilities/ValidationTool.cs), which throws the first error message.
- UI patterns: Forms construct services through InstanceFactory in constructors. ProductForm handles add/update in one dialog using IProductService; CustomerForm does grid-bound CRUD; SalesForm seeds a customer row Id=0 labeled "Walk-in" and nulls CustomerId when saving. Main grid loads ProductDetailDto, search uses GetProductDetailsByName.
- Reporting: [InventoryFlow.UI/Reports/ExcelReporter.cs](../InventoryFlow.UI/Reports/ExcelReporter.cs) uses ClosedXML; callers pass a non-empty List<ProductDetailDto>, choose SaveFileDialog path, and columns auto-fit.
- Data conventions: decimal for money, int for quantities; Business layer sets AddedDate/Date; DAL stays free of business checks.
- Migrations: stored under InventoryFlow.DataAccess/Migrations. Run from repo root: `dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project InventoryFlow.DataAccess --startup-project InventoryFlow.UI` then `dotnet ef database update --project InventoryFlow.DataAccess --startup-project InventoryFlow.UI`.
- CRUD expectations: managers expect Id set for delete/update. UI refreshes grids after dialogs/operations (LoadProducts/LoadSalesHistory/LoadCustomers).
